finding: Concurrent JSON readers and atomic replacement can fail under ordinary Windows file-sharing semantics.

captured_before_fix.experiment: Held ordinary reader during atomic_json replacement; actual OS call
Two real export workers while parent polls get_result every 50 ms; failed second batch

subsequent_launcher_probe.experiment: Popen current venv interpreter running a child that reports os.getpid(); wait for normal exit
subsequent_launcher_probe.implication: Killing and waiting for the launcher handle does not by itself prove the executing worker has released its handles.

remediation.scope: Windows EACCES PermissionError with absent winerror or winerror 5, 32, 33 around JSON read and metadata replacement only

limits: The unexplained v0.4 timeout was not reproduced and its cause remains unknown.

This early trial killed the owned Popen handle. A later probe confirmed Windows venv launcher PID differs from interpreter PID; direct interpreter-death fault injection is required for the final recovery evidence.
Blocking filesystem calls may exceed the nominal sleep budget; cooperative export deadlines are still checked before publication.
Finite tiny-fixture process trials are not Elasticsearch, large-dataset throughput, tail-latency or agent-accuracy evidence.
Desktop load and filesystem cache uncontrolled; diagnosis receipts contain no raw records, exception messages or machine paths.
